originalTitle: Zomi Frankcom: Penny Wong condemns ‘insulting’ decision to clear IDF over Gaza strikes that killed Australian aid worker
summary: Foreign affairs minister says Australia is ‘outraged’ after Israeli government decided not to pursue criminal proceedings over 2024 triple drone strike on humanitarian convoy
content: Australia’s foreign affairs minister has expressed “outrage” and will call in the Israeli ambassador over the Israel Defense Forces decision overnight not to open a criminal investigation into Gaza strikes that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom. In a statement released on Thursday, Penny Wong called the timing of the decision, on World Humanitarian Day, “especially insulting”. Wong said she would call in Israel’s ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, for formal talks and directed Australia’s ambassador to Israel, Neil Hawkins, “to convey our views directly to Israel as the Australian government considers next steps”. The April 2024 strike hit a convoy of World Central Kitchen vehicles, killing seven humanitarian workers from the US-based aid group, which has distributed food in Gaza throughout the war. The aid group said at the time it had coordinated with the military over the movement of its cars. The vehicles, which had the group’s logo on their roofs visible from the air, were left incinerated and mangled, indicating a series of targeted strikes. The IDF said on Wednesday it had mistaken several individuals in the vehicles for armed Hamas military operatives, and that the convoy deviated from the previously coordinated route. It concluded that “the decisions of the commanders did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct”. Two officers were removed from their positions at the time and three others reprimanded. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email One of those killed in the strike was Frankcom, an Australian aid worker. The Australian government has previously called the deaths a “tragedy and an outrage” and pressed for full accountability and “any appropriate criminal charges”. In February the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said he had made it clear to Israel and its president, Isaac Herzog, that Australia expected transparency about Israel’s then-ongoing investigation into the incident. “Australia is outraged the Israeli Government has decided not to pursue criminal proceedings against those responsible for killing Zomi Frankcom and her World Central Kitchen colleagues,” Wong said in her Thursday morning statement. “The Australian government learned of Israel’s decision late last night, moments before it was announced, on World Humanitarian Day – which is especially insulting to Zomi’s loved ones, humanitarians and all Australians. “Zomi represented the best of Australia. Her courage deserves to be celebrated. Her family deserves justice.” Wong said the move “falls far short of the accountability we expect”. “This is despite Israel Defense Forces admissions that the IDF strikes on Zomi and her colleagues’ vehicles were the result of serious failures to follow IDF procedures, mistaken identification and errors in decision-making.” This was confirmed by special adviser air chief marshal Mark Binskin’s report, Wong said. “Democracies seek and accept higher standards. The Australian Government will not stop pressing Israel for justice for Zomi and her colleagues.” World Central Kitchen said it strongly disagreed with Israeli officials’ account of the airstrikes and their decision not to pursue a criminal investigation. “There has never been any excuse or justification for the attacks, and there is nothing in this account that does so. The decision is inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive,” it said in a statement. “At the time of the lethal attacks, the IDF knew that our team in Gaza was unarmed and posing a threat to nobody. It had full visual clarity on our clearly marked humanitarian vehicles during the extended, multiple airstrikes. It knew our team’s movements, identities and activities in advance.” Human rights expert Chris Sidoti said the federal government should send Newman, the Israeli ambassador, home. Sidoti, a former human rights commissioner, was a member of the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel. “The minister, when she sees the ambassador, should tell him that he’s going home. I don’t support breaking diplomatic relations with Israel. I don’t support the closing of embassies, but this bloke is clearly an unacceptable representative.” The Greens leader, Larissa Waters, demanded Israel’s government be hit with new sanctions. “Now, strong words are not enough,” she told ABC radio on Thursday. “The Australian government sending some strongly worded statements has meant nothing. Now it is time that the Australian government puts on sanctions against the state of Israel and stops sending weapons parts to this genocide.” In April this year, Wong paid tribute to Frankcom on the second anniversary of her death, saying “people like Zomi are rare and their selflessness should not only be celebrated but protected”.
chineseTitle: Zomi Frankcom：黄英贤谴责以色列国防军就加沙袭击导致澳大利亚援助人员死亡的“侮辱性”决定
chineseSummary: 外交部长表示，以色列政府决定不对 2024 年人道主义车队遭受的三重无人机袭击提起刑事诉讼，澳大利亚对此感到“愤怒”
chineseContent: 澳大利亚外交部长对此表示“愤怒”，并将传唤以色列大使，因为以色列国防军连夜决定不对导致澳大利亚援助人员佐米·弗兰克科姆死亡的加沙袭击展开刑事调查。在周四发布的一份声明中，黄英贤称，在世界人道主义日做出这一决定的时机“尤其具有侮辱性”。黄表示，她将召集以色列驻澳大利亚大使希勒尔·纽曼进行正式会谈，并指示澳大利亚驻以色列大使尼尔·霍金斯“在澳大利亚政府考虑下一步行动时直接向以色列传达我们的观点”。 2024 年 4 月的罢工袭击了世界中央厨房车队，导致美国援助组织的 7 名人道主义工作人员死亡，该组织在整个战争期间一直在加沙分发食物。该援助组织当时表示，已就车辆的调动问题与军方进行了协调。这些车辆的车顶上有该组织的标志，从空中清晰可见，这些车辆被焚烧和毁坏，表明遭到了一系列有针对性的袭击。以色列国防军周三表示，它误将车辆中的几人误认为是哈马斯武装军事人员，并且车队偏离了之前协调的路线。其结论是“指挥官的决定并未引起对不当犯罪行为的合理怀疑”。当时，两名警官被免职，另外三名警官受到谴责。注册澳大利亚突发新闻电子邮件 在罢工中丧生的人之一是澳大利亚救援人员 Frankcom。澳大利亚政府此前曾称这些死亡事件是“悲剧和愤慨”，并敦促追究全部责任并提出“任何适当的刑事指控”。二月，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内 (Anthony Albane)
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
